terms.comment: The wand with which Circe turns men into beasts and back again, and Mercury’s, with which he calls up souls and gives or takes away sleep; Lewis & Short gives “a magic wand” as a sense of its own. Circe’s is golden in Vergil, aurea virga.

phrases.latin: Virgā tē tangam, et in rānam vertēris!
phrases.english: I’ll touch you with my magic wand, and you’ll turn into a frog!

phrases.latin: Pīcus, … quem capta cupīdine conjūnx aurea percussum virgā versumque venēnīs fēcit avem Circē sparsitque colōribus ālās
phrases.english: Picus, whom his wife Circe, seized with desire, struck with her golden wand, changed with her potions into a bird, and spattered his wings with colours

phrases.latin: percutimurque caput conversae verbere virgae, verbaque dīcuntur dictīs contrāria verbīs
phrases.english: and we are struck on the head with the wand turned round, and words are spoken against the words she had said

sources: Lewis & Short: virga
